site_venue: Grassroots Centre, Memorial Park, Memorial Avenue, London E15 3DB
site_activity: Weekly stay-and-play sessions for mothers and children under five living in temporary or insecure accommodation, combining a supported play session with a baby/nappy bank, children's clothes bank, hot meals, travel expenses, breastfeeding support and enrichment (art, messy play, music, dance), alongside on-site advice from Shelter housing advisers, health visitors and children's-centre family support workers
last_delivery_what: Launched research report 'Help and Hope on Hold', with Magpie Mums calling for better access to SEND services
local_trigger: Almost 2,000 under-fives live in temporary accommodation in Newham (per Nesta New Radicals 2018 feature)
lived_experience_governance: Former service users ('Magpie Mums') with lived experience of temporary accommodation sit on the REACH (Rights, Experience, Advocacy, Change) team and on the mums' steering committee; some volunteer, and one is employed by the charity (per themagpieproject.org/contact/ and /home-2/).

_certifications_note: APPLICANT-SUPPLIED CERTIFICATIONS (not from public materials): the four boolean administrative self-certifications below are what a real applicant attests on the intake form and are not published anywhere. They are set true here because all four are established registered charities delivering services to vulnerable people, for whom a safeguarding policy, public liability insurance, own-name banking and a conflict-free application are universal and, for safeguarding, legally expected. No specific unknowable detail (e.g. a named Designated Safeguarding Lead) is invented — those stay blank.
